newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Japan lawmakers set security forum.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Japan lawmakers set security forum.

text.p: Lawmakers from Taiwan and Japan have agreed to form a security forum to discuss regional defence and security policies, local media said on Sunday.
A Taiwan delegation led by parliamentary deputy speaker Wang Jin-pyng reached the agreement with its Japanese counterpart during a recent visit to Tokyo, the United Daily News said.
Taiwan's delegation, which returned on Saturday, met prominent lawmakers and ministerial-level officials during its four-day stay in Japan, the report said.
The forum would represent a channel for dialogue on regional security matters in the absence of diplomatic ties between Taipei and Tokyo, the paper quoted lawmakers as saying.
Wang was quoted by the China Times Express as saying the first Taiwan-Japan secuity forum would be held in July or August.
Taiwan and Japan did not rule out the possibility of inviting other countries to take part in the forum, it quoted Wang as saying.
Japanese and Taiwan lawmakers would try to influence their governments' security policies help build up a security system in the Asia-Pacific region, it said.
The report gave no details of how the forum would function.

Tokyo recognises Taipei's arch rival in Beijing as the only legitimate Chinese government but maintains close unofficial ties with the island it ruled as a colony for a half century before Japan's World War Two defeat in 1945.
Beijing has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and vows to attack if it strays from its avowed goal of unification and opts for independence.
Taiwan's leaders have voiced concern over China's growing military power and advocates an Asia-Pacific security system to counter the communist Chinese threat.
